sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force 13 December 2020)
Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Trade Agreement (in force)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement between Vanuatu and Australia (in force 2010)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement between Vanuatu and New Zealand (in force 2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 43 of 2015, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit Act No. 34 of 2000, as amended; International Companies Act No. 20 of 1992, as amended (beneficial ownership record-keeping and register obligations); Companies Act [Cap. 191], as amended (UBO provisions for domestic companies); International Service Providers (Licensing) Act No. 8 of 2009, as amended; VFSC AML/CFT Rules and Beneficial Ownership Guidelines issued under the AML/CFT Act 2015

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Office or National Identity Authority of the document holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu is a Contracting Party; non-member states require Consular Legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on source jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the banking relationship and corroborating source of funds of each subscriber/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille by the issuing bank's competent supervisory authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and register of directors/UBOs of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry/registrar of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; non-Hague jurisdictions require Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of UBO structure signed by each shareholder/director (UBO Declaration Form of the licensed registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu-licensed registered agent administered under the International Service Providers (Licensing) Act 2009
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Vanuatu; Apostille not required if executed before a Vanuatu notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU/UK Consolidated Financial Sanctions Targets, and the Vanuatu Domestic Designated Persons list maintained by the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT Act 2015. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), requiring independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds at onboarding and at least every 12 months thereafter. Negative news and adverse-media screening, ongoing transaction monitoring, and sanctions re-screening at each material change of ownership are mandatory for licensed registered agents.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Company Name Search and Reservation service via licensed registered agents (online portal access at https://www.vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages are Bislama, English, and French; names must be expressed in Latin script. A name in a non-Latin script may be adopted only where a Latin-script transliteration is submitted and accepted by the Registrar. The proposed name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any name already registered with the VFSC or the local Companies Registry, and must comply with the naming conventions of the International Companies Act 1992.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant's licensed registered agent may: (1) obtain a written statement of reasons from the Registrar within 14 days of the refusal date; (2) file a written administrative reconsideration application with the VFSC Registrar within 21 days of the refusal, supported by legal submissions addressing each ground of refusal; (3) if the reconsideration is declined, apply to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu for judicial review within 30 days of the reconsideration decision; and (4) in parallel, submit an amended name application (new fee payable) to avoid delay. Sensitive-token names require prior written consent of the relevant minister or licensing authority (e.g., Reserve Bank of Vanuatu for 'Bank' or 'Finance' tokens; VFSC for insurance, securities, and fiduciary tokens).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office at the premises of a VFSC-licensed registered agent in Port Vila is permissible as the statutory registered office of an International Company under the International Companies Act 1992. However, for the ISIC 5224 bulk-port stevedoring operational license, the Vanuatu Maritime Authority / Ports and Marine Department will require a demonstrable physical commercial presence in Vanuatu, including a terminal operating agreement or port-services contract; a virtual office alone is therefore insufficient for the operational license phase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High (approximately 45-65% likelihood) for a licensed stevedoring operator: unannounced spot inspections may be conducted by the Vanuatu Maritime Authority, the Vanuatu Ports and Marine Department, and the VFSC under its anti-money laundering supervision powers; registered offices and operational port facilities are both subject to inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap 222] of the Republic of Vanuatu, ss.6-10 (incorporation), s.7 (memorandum of association), s.12 (registered agent), s.108 (registered office); supplementary procedural rules under the International Companies Regulations and VFSC guidance notes. The domestic Companies Act [Cap 191] does not apply to International Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Registration as an International Company, together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and the Registered Agent's Declaration of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Vanuatu International Company. The authorised capital is fixed in the Memorandum of Association (market convention commonly sets USD 1,000 to USD 50,000), and shares may be issued for cash or other consideration in any currency. No escrow account, bank deposit, or physical capital deposit is mandated by VFSC for standard licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of [Company Name], a Vanuatu International Company. RESOLVED, that: (1) the subscriber share subscription contained in the Memorandum of Association is ratified, shares are allotted to subscribers, and consideration is recorded in the register of members; (2) the registered office is fixed at the registered agent's address in Port Vila, Vanuatu, under Section 108 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222]; (3) the subscriber is appointed sole director, and [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, to hold office until the next annual general meeting; (4) the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, appoint the registered agent, and take all actions necessary to perfect incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search through a VFSC-licensed registered agent against the National Companies Register. Submit a written Name Reservation Request to the Corporate Registry; the Registry verifies that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, protected name, or prohibited symbol under Section 7 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222]. A reservation is held for a defined statutory window, during which the incorporation documents must be filed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of corporate subscriber (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the registered agent may resubmit up to three alternative names without additional government fee within the same calendar month; the reservation date is reset upon acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarisation of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed Registered Agent, Port Vila, Vanuatu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English setting out the company name, registered office clause, object clause covering international stevedoring, bulk cargo terminal operations and marine logistics, authorised share capital, and subscriber particulars. Each subscriber signs the Memorandum and Articles before a witness; signatures executed outside Vanuatu may be notarised or apostilled. The Registered Agent certifies the statutory documents as compliant prior to filing.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of each director and officer
Power of attorney or corporate resolution where subscriber is a body corporate
Notarised identification of overseas signatories (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Draft deficiencies are cured by issuing a revised execution page; subscribers re-sign only the amended page to avoid full re-execution and re-notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Registration Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Filing Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form IC-1 (Application for Registration as an International Company) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, declarations of compliance, and proof of fee payment. The filing is submitted electronically through the VFSC portal or physically via the licensed registered agent. The statutory fee of USD 350 is settled by wire transfer to the VFSC official bank account or at the VFSC counter. The Commission stamps the application and issues an acknowledgment receipt.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Compliance signed by the Registered Agent
Consent to Act forms of directors and officers
Receipt or proof of statutory filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC issues a requisition under Section 13 of the Act, the applicant has 30 days to file a corrective amendment; failure to cure results in deemed withdrawal of the application with a proportionate refund available on written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Commencement of Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of all statutory conditions, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing a unique VFSC registration number. The company becomes a body corporate with limited liability as of the certificate date. The Registered Agent then opens the statutory registers of members, directors, officers, and charges as required by the International Companies Act [Cap 222].
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the Certificate of Incorporation are rectified by written application under Section 209 of the Act; the amended certificate is reissued without a new incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Engaging the Licensed Registered Agent in Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed Registered Agent, Port Vila, Vanuatu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Registered Agent and Registered Office Service Agreement; instruct the agent to file the Notice of Registered Office Address with the VFSC under Section 108 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222]. The board ratifies the registered office address in the First Board Resolution, and the agent accepts service of process and all official correspondence on behalf of the company.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office Address (Form R-4)
Executed copy of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any subsequent change of registered office is lodged by the agent on Form R-4 within 30 days; late filing penalties are avoided by submission before the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Shares, Seal, and Establishment of Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Secretary / Registered Agent acting under the direction of the Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Allot the subscriber shares reflected in the register of members, issue share certificates, and adopt the common seal where the board elects to use one. Open the statutory corporate minute book and governance files; record the share allotment, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Minutes and resolutions must be maintained in English in accordance with the Act for inspection by VFSC and third-party due diligence.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and resolutions folder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective share certificates are cancelled and reissued upon board approval; minute corrections are effected by chair initialling and a dated correction footnote.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Ports and Harbours, Ministry of Infrastructure and Public Utilities, Republic of Vanuatu, acting jointly with the Vanuatu Maritime Authority for vessel interface operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Stevedoring Terminal Operator Licence (Bulk Cargo Handling and Marine Dock Loading/Unloading Permit)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Environment, Energy and Disaster Management, Republic of Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Preliminary Environmental Assessment (PEA) mandatory for bulk port terminal construction and stevedoring operations; escalation to Category A Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is required where daily throughput exceeds 5,000 tonnes, where the wharf receives vessels above 5,000 DWT, or where the cargo includes substances listed as hazardous under the Waste Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Water Resource Management Act and the Pollution Control Regulations: treated process wastewater and ballast discharge must not exceed total suspended solids 50 mg/L and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) 30 mg/L; dust suppression and covered conveyor systems must keep ambient particulate matter (PM10) below WHO guideline values; all bulk cargo residues and washwater are segregated and disposed through a DEPC-approved waste facility; bunker fuel and oil handling must meet the Petroleum Act spill-response thresholds and IMO ballast water management standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services (VFES); wharf structural load and crane foundation certification by the Department of Public Works; Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) registration with the Department of Labour under the Workplace Health and Safety Act, including stevedoring risk assessments; inspection and registration of all mobile cranes, conveyor systems, and lifting gear under national equipment registration rules; emergency response and pollution contingency clearance coordinated with the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) for terminal operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) is the sole registrar and regulator of International Companies (ICs); fiscal and customs administration is vested in Vanuatu Customs & Inland Revenue (VCIR) within the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM). No general income-tax administration exists because Vanuatu imposes no national income, profits, capital-gains, or withholding taxes. Statutory e-portal: https://www.vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is issued to ICs. The VFSC company registration number on the Certificate of Incorporation serves as the sole fiscal identifier. Procedure for a foreign-owned IC: (1) engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent; (2) file the Memorandum and Articles through the VFSC e-portal; (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation bearing a unique company number; (4) file the annual exemption declaration and pay the VFSC annual government fee; (5) if any narrow domestic fiscal obligation arises (employer registration for locally resident staff or a customs account for imported terminal equipment), apply to VCIR for a TIN using the Certificate of Incorporation, a registered-agent letter, and CRS/FATCA self-certification. ICs are not registered with VCIR by default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Exempt-status election is made at incorporation under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]: all profits, income, capital gains, dividends, and distributions of an IC are exempt from all present and future Vanuatu taxes, duties, and stamp duty, provided the IC does not carry on business with Vanuatu residents or transact in Vatu currency. No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections exist in Vanuatu law. Optional statutory conversions are available: IC-to-local-company and local-company-to-IC (Part 12 of the IC Act), each requiring VFSC approval. No distribution tax, no withholding tax, and no thin-capitalization or interest-disallowance regime applies to ICs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No National VAT/GST/Sales-and-Use Tax (import customs duty and import infrastructure tax arise only at the border)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no consumption-tax regime, no turnover threshold, and no VAT registration requirement exists in Vanuatu; municipal business-license fees apply only to onshore trading activities, from which an IC is statutorily barred.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Vanuatu imposes no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control obligation. Stevedoring invoices may be issued in any agreed commercial form; SWIFT wire and Port Authority clearing rails are the operative settlement evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable by VAT mechanics: Vanuatu has no VAT/GST, so there is no 0% export rate and no input-tax refund pathway. The operative relief is the IC statutory exemption itself: all earnings of an IC, including stevedoring revenue from international bulk vessels, are fully exempt from Vanuatu taxation. Exemption is preserved only where stevedoring services are contracted by, invoiced to, and paid by non-resident shipowners or charterers in foreign currency (offshore business). Services rendered to Vanuatu resident principals or paid in Vatu breach the domestic-business prohibition and destroy exempt status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration/export entry for the underlying bulk cargo
Bill of Lading evidencing carriage on an international voyage
Port/terminal stevedoring service contract with a non-resident carrier, charterer, or P&I-appointed surveyor
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit voucher for overseas freight and handling fees
Cargo manifest and tally sheets endorsed by the Vanuatu Ports Authority
VFSC annual return with tax-exemption declaration and payment receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback can arise because no consumption tax is in force. Vanuatu maintains no exchange controls, so the 0-day entry denotes the absence of any statutory FX-repatriation deadline rather than a same-day remittance requirement. Enforcement risk concentrates on the IC exempt-status conditions: knowingly carrying on domestic (onshore) business in Vatu with Vanuatu residents exposes the company to fines, loss of the statutory tax exemption, retrospective assessment of customs and municipal liabilities, VFSC deregistration, and mandatory re-registration as a local company; false declarations to VFSC are prosecutable offenses against both the company and its officers. Commercial export documentation (bill of lading, inward remittance, manifests) remains the standard audit trail for VFSC, VCIR, and bank AML review of port-terminal cash flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) – The national monetary authority established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [CAP 125]; regulates foreign exchange dealing, payment and settlement systems, and licensed banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu operates an open foreign exchange regime with no exchange controls or surrender requirements on current or capital account transactions. The VUV is a managed-float currency linked to a trade-weighted SDR/partner-currency basket. There are no restrictions on repatriation of profits, dividends, or capital for bona fide trade or investment transactions. All cross-border settlements are subject to anti-money laundering (AML) due diligence and reporting of international transfers by the servicing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export receipts. Foreign-currency earnings from stevedoring and port services may be held offshore or in designated foreign-currency accounts at Vanuatu banks. There is no statutory timeline or minimum conversion ratio; exporters may convert at their discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. Vanuatu law does not provide for a dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) or digital bank licence class. Offshore EMIs can receive funds from foreign counterparties but cannot clear VUV-denominated payments or settle through the local Automated Transfer System (ATS). Use of unregulated EMIs as the primary banking rail is not advisable due to VFSC registration requirements under the Financial Dealers Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for International Companies where all signatories hold recognised nationality passports (excluding high-risk countries) and documents are notarised and apostilled/localised by the Vanuatu Commissioner of Oaths. However, most Tier 1 banks require at least one natural person director or authorized signatory to attend a physical KYC interview at the Port Vila branch, or to provide a certified Skype/Teams interview with the bank's compliance officer. Non-resident directors may rely on locally appointed company secretaries for in-person onboarding, subject to enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete UBO chain for non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate chart with beneficial ownership identification (name, DOB, nationality and residential address) for every holder of 10% or more; original share certificates; board resolution appointing account signatories; certified passports; utility bills less than 6 months old; and a certificate of good standing of the International Company from the VFSC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds concern for large capital injection or escrow funding from a tax-haven jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or an asset and liability statement certified by a licensed CPA; source-of-wealth explanation letter covering the prior 24-month period; bank statements from the remitting bank evidencing legitimate accumulation; sale/purchase agreements or inheritance affidavits; and a legal opinion letter from a Vanuatu law firm confirming the IC's tax-exempt status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (Politically Exposed Person) indicator on a director, shareholder, or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP clearance certificate issued by a licensed due diligence provider; sworn affidavit of the PEP explaining the commercial rationale for the account; evidence of genuine operating history in the maritime/port sector; and an independent probity report prepared by a Vanuatu-licensed accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound investor capital must be routed through a SWIFT MT103 credit message to the bank account registered in the name of VU_IC. The payment should reference purpose code 'GIT' (General Investment) or 'CAPG' (Capital Goods and Materials) and include the Unique Investor Code issued by VIPA if the underlying project is classified as a foreign investment. The bank will require a board resolution from the IC authorising the account opening and deposit, an updated share register evidencing issued shares, and a source-of-funds declaration from the remitting shareholder. Funds originating from sanctioned or high-risk countries may require an additional legal letter and RBV notification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound commitments (vessel agency fees, port handling royalties, equipment lease payments, and supplier invoices) are settled via: (i) standard SWIFT MT103 – for fiat transfers under USD/VUV 1,000,000 transaction threshold; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit – for large capital imports of cranes/terminal machinery, with accepted currencies USD, EUR, AUD, NZD and JPY; and (iii) interbank VUV clearing through the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu's Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) system for domestic payables. All MT103 messages must be accompanied by underlying trade documentation (invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration) to satisfy RBV AML reporting requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward foreign-exchange contracts with a licensed authorised dealer, allowing fixed-rate locking of up to 12 months for genuine trade or investment exposure.
Cross-currency swaps between VUV and major trade-partner currencies (USD, AUD, NZD, EUR) executed with the prior approval of the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu.
FX swaps with the same counterparty for rollover of short-term trade financing, subject to RBV spot/forward split confirmation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Company Confirmation Statement (International Companies Act Cap 222, s.101)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately USD 45 per month or part thereof; failure to file within 3 months of the anniversary triggers VFSC administrative strike-off proceedings, with dissolution gazetted within 6 to 12 months and assets vesting in the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) filed through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrently with the Annual Return; any change of agent or office must be lodged within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent or to notify changes renders the International Company non-compliant; directors are jointly and severally liable to a penalty of approximately USD 900 under the International Companies Act, and continued absence of an agent leads to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance and Activity Declaration (annual attestation for internationally active port-terminal holding operations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Economic Substance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Although Vanuatu International Companies are tax-exempt, a false or omitted substance declaration exposes the company and its directors to VFSC investigation, monetary penalties, and disqualification; no separate government filing fee is imposed for this declaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation submitted via the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) under the Companies and Trust Service Providers Act No. 23 of 2022
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal within the same 30-day anniversary window; the agent must update VFSC within 5 business days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance attracts fines of up to approximately USD 90,000 for the registered agent and USD 45,000 for the company; persistent default triggers reclassification as a shell entity and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Agent Compliance Certificate (certifying registered office, registered agent, and statutory registers are in good standing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) included in the Annual Return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the Annual Return (30 days post-anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficiencies in the compliance certificate expose the registered agent to regulatory sanctions; an International Company without a compliant authorized agent is subject to administrative strike-off within 6 months.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. Vanuatu International Companies are statutorily exempt from independent audit under the International Companies Act Cap 222, regardless of turnover, total assets, or shareholder count. A mandatory audit may arise only if the VFSC Registrar directs one following an inspection or if the company's own articles of association require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory IFRS or Local GAAP. The International Company must maintain accounting records under s.40 of the International Companies Act Cap 222 that correctly explain transactions and enable the financial position to be determined with reasonable accuracy; such records may be kept outside Vanuatu with the registered agent's consent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The VFSC-licensed registered agent must collect and verify beneficial ownership data annually during the incorporation-anniversary cycle. Under the Companies and Trust Service Providers Act No. 23 of 2022 and VFSC AML/CFT rules, the agent reconciles the UBO electronic record against the on-site Register of Members; any share transfer, allotment, or change of control must be reported by the directors to the agent within 14 days and embedded in the next annual confirmation. A transfer of 10% or more of the share capital triggers enhanced due diligence but remains tax-neutral because the International Company is tax-exempt.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 1,800 for a licensed VFSC registered agent, inclusive of compliance officer and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute. Voluntary operational audit by an international CPA firm for a bulk port stevedoring International Company: USD 5,000 - 8,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no dividend or interest withholding tax is imposed in Vanuatu. International Companies are expressly exempt from Vanuatu income taxation and are subject only to prescribed VFSC annual registration/renewal fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return form exists. International Companies file an annual confirmation/renewal through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) online portal; no domestic tax return is prescribed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (VFSC compliance renewal); no quarterly or annual corporate income tax filing requirement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: VFSC annual renewal is due on or before the anniversary of incorporation; no statutory deadline is tied to a fiscal year-end because no income tax return is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of registered agent, registered office address, directors, shareholders, authorized capital, and payment of the annual VFSC fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders may be listed without a Vanuatu tax identification number; all filings must be submitted through the licensed Vanuatu registered agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal attracts reinstatement and restoration fees under VFSC practice and may lead to striking-off/deregistration. No corporate income tax late-filing surcharge applies because no corporate income tax return is filed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double-tax agreement network and no domestic treaty-relief claim procedure. Dividend distributions from a Vanuatu International Company are paid gross, with no Vanuatu withholding, no Tax Residency Certificate requirement, and no source-country tax credit available inside Vanuatu.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding rate on royalties and interest; no DTA rate applies. Vanuatu levies no withholding tax on cross-border IP royalties or debt interest paid by an International Company.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable; Vanuatu does not impose corporate income tax and has not enacted transfer-pricing documentation thresholds in Vanuatu vatu (VUV). No Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Report is required of an International Company.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No Economic Substance Regulations are currently in force in Vanuatu. However, an International Company must maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Vanuatu, and should retain corporate minutes and records to demonstrate separate legal personality and validity of the offshore structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Domestic Business by an International Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a bulk port stevedoring terminal in Vanuatu, providing loading/unloading services to Vanuatu-resident counterparties, or holding/using Vanuatu land or facilities in breach of the International Company's non-resident status and applicable port/business licensing requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Striking-off or deregistration by VFSC, forfeiture of exemption benefits, cessation orders by the Ports Authority, and penalties under the International Companies Act and Vanuatu business licensing legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent may be subject to enforcement proceedings; a court may pierce the corporate veil if the International Company is used as a sham to conduct domestic trade, exposing directors to civil liability for debts and losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppressing 12.5% value-added tax on taxable stevedoring or ancillary port services, filing false import declarations for terminal equipment and fuel, or using an International Company exemption to avoid customs duties on goods entering Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid VAT/customs duty, statutory interest, monetary penalties, seizure and forfeiture of goods, and criminal prosecution under the VAT Act and Customs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors can be prosecuted personally; failure to account for public money may trigger personal restitution orders, asset freezing, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing port-terminal payments, Swift wires, or Port Authority clearing transactions through Vanuatu to hide criminal proceeds, or failing to implement AML/CFT controls required by Vanuatu's supervisory and financial-intelligence framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC administrative penalties, suspension or revocation of licenses, reporting to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit, and criminal fines or imprisonment under Vanuatu's AML/CFT legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors who knowingly facilitate laundering may face criminal liability, personal fines, travel bans, and court-ordered confiscation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Trading and False Statements to VFSC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making false declarations to VFSC regarding directors, shareholders, registered office, or business objects; conducting business with intent to defraud creditors or foreign revenue authorities through fictitious stevedoring invoices or sham corporate records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties for false statements, deregistration, winding-up proceedings, disqualification orders against directors, and compulsory restoration fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fraudulent trading and losses suffered by creditors; the corporate veil may be pierced where the International Company is simply a façade, leading to personal fines, disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Offshore Arrangement for Foreign Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Vanuatu International Company to conceal foreign-source income, fabricate stevedoring charges, or obscure beneficial ownership of port-terminal cash flows in jurisdictions imposing corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu cooperates through tax information exchange agreements and mutual legal assistance mechanisms; domestic tax exemption does not protect the arrangement from lawful foreign tax investigations, freezing orders, or enforcement requests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and directors remain liable under applicable foreign tax law; Vanuatu courts may assist with asset freezing, evidence production, and enforcement where the arrangement is fraudulent.
